roadmap.goal: Before anything is persisted, a Portfolio owner can see what a Jira Release would give them: which Releases this connection offers, which of them carry a date, and which Features would come along.

validation.findings: 1 BLOCKER, 3 HIGH (all clean), 3 MEDIUM, 3 LOW (all clean)

orchestrator_corrections: ResolveMany pulled into slice 01a as step 01-04. The draft left it throwing and gave preview its own membership query, which spells the fixVersion JQL twice and leaves one copy to delete in slice 02.
AC-01.6 had no coverage at all in the draft.
DeliveryService.test.ts was missing from the precursor file list although it calls create positionally at :215.

phases.name: Make room in the modal before adding a tab

steps.name: Descriptor-driven selection tabs and a create options object
steps.scenario_name: The Manual and Rule-based tabs still render, switch, validate and save exactly as they did before
criteria: A new deliverySelectionTabs.ts exports a DeliverySelectionTab descriptor list, and DeliveryCreateModal reads the tab list from it at every site that today branches on the hardcoded Manual/RuleBased pair.
All eight branch sites are converted: the ButtonGroup, SelectionModeContent, getFirstBlockingError, isSaveDisabled, the payload builder, the edit-hydration effect and the reset.
IDeliveryService.create takes a single IDeliveryCreateOptions object instead of seven positional parameters, matching the shape update already uses.
The mock delivery service and the single production call site are updated to the options object.
DeliveryCreateModal.test.tsx, DeliveryCreateModal.edit.test.tsx and DeliveryCreateModal.rulebased.test.tsx all pass with no edit to any of the three files.
pnpm test green, pnpm build with zero errors and zero warnings, Biome clean.
This lands as one refactor commit, separate from every feature commit that follows.

The three existing DeliveryCreateModal suites are the control: if any of them needs editing, the refactor changed behaviour and has failed - revert rather than adjust the test. DeliveryCreateModal.tsx is 794 lines; the branch sites are around the ButtonGroup at :673-713, SelectionModeContent at :716-739, getFirstBlockingError at :754 and isSaveDisabled at :779, plus the payload builder, the edit-hydration effect and the reset. IDeliveryService is declared at DeliveryService.ts:50 and mocked by createMockDeliveryService at src/tests/MockApiServiceProvider.ts:391. The only production caller of create is useDeliveryManagement.ts:232 inside handleCreateDelivery. The maintainer settled that both parts land in the SAME precursor commit - do not split them. Verified call sites: useDeliveryManagement.ts:232 is the only production caller of create, and DeliveryService.test.ts:215 the only test caller. The three DeliveryCreateModal suites do not call it directly, which is why they must pass untouched.

phases.name: The Jira adapter learns to list its Releases

steps.name: Let the bindability specs run
criteria: The Ignore attribute carrying the DISTILL scaffold message is removed from all four specs.
A_live_source_carrying_a_date_can_be_bound passes.
A_source_with_no_date_is_offered_but_says_what_is_missing passes.
A_retired_source_cannot_be_bound_even_when_it_has_a_date passes.
A_retired_source_with_no_date_reports_being_retired passes.
No production file is touched by this step.
steps.implementation_notes: DeliverySourceBindability is already fully implemented, not a stub - DISTILL landed both the type and its four specs, and the specs pass the moment the attribute comes off. The four methods sit at DeliverySourceBindabilityTest.cs L24-33, L36-47, L50-61 and L64-71. This is deliberately the first backend commit: it turns the DISTILL contract surface from decoration into a live signal before anything is built on it, so a later regression in the grading rule has somewhere to fail. If any of the four does NOT pass once un-ignored, stop and report rather than editing the production type - that would mean DISTILL and DESIGN disagree about the grading rule. Expect no build warnings; run the suite with the live-connector categories excluded.

steps.name: Jira offers its Releases; the other four systems offer nothing
steps.scenario_name: A Jira connection offers its Releases as a delivery source
criteria: AvailableSources returns a single DeliverySourceDescriptor for Jira Releases instead of throwing.
The descriptor's display name uses the literal Jira concept, Release, and not a Terminology-configurable word.
SupportsDeliveryForecastPublishing and PublishAsync are left throwing NotImplementedException with the existing private const; those two belong to the outbound slices.
The new spec class carries no Category attribute, so it runs in the default filtered test pass.
AvailableSources performs no I/O and is a pure function of the connection it is handed.
Nothing is added to the shared IWorkTrackingConnector port.
steps.implementation_notes: The five provider stubs sit at the bottom of JiraWorkTrackingConnector.cs: AvailableSources L1955-1958, GetOptions L1960-1963, ResolveMany L1965-1969, SupportsDeliveryForecastPublishing L1971-1974, PublishAsync L1976-1980. Slice 01a implements AvailableSources and GetOptions here and ResolveMany in step 01-04; the two publishing stubs stay throwing, and the shared literal stays behind the existing private const because S1192 already fired once on those five strings. IMPORTANT: do NOT put these specs in JiraWorkTrackingConnectorTest.cs - that class is decorated [Category("Integration")] and [Category("JiraIntegration")] at :12-13, which the mandatory local and CI test filter excludes, so a spec added there would silently never run. A new uncategorised JiraDeliverySourceProviderTest.cs is the right home. No IDeliverySourceHandler and no IDeliverySourceRegistry is introduced - the composed IDeliverySourceProvider on IJiraWorkTrackingConnector is the shipped shape, and the four non-Jira systems degrade by simply not implementing the interface. CA1859: any new non-public helper takes the concrete type, never the interface.

steps.name: Read the project versions and grade each one
steps.scenario_name: A Release with no release date is offered but cannot be selected
criteria: GetOptions issues GET rest/api/3/project/{key}/versions through the connector's existing authenticated client and returns one DeliverySourceOption per version.
The payload-to-option mapping is a pure function in its own reader type, exercised against a captured versions payload with no network call.
A version whose releaseDate key is absent yields an option with no date; absent is treated as no date, never as a parse failure.
Selectability comes from DeliverySourceBindability.For(hasDate, isRetiredAtSource), so the server decides and a direct POST cannot bind what the picker greys out.
archived true means not selectable; released true stays selectable.
An unknown or unoffered source key is rejected before any HTTP call is made.
The suite stays green with the live-connector categories excluded, and the build carries zero warnings.
steps.implementation_notes: Slice 00 confirmed the versions response carries self, id, name, archived, released, projectId, and releaseDate ONLY when a date is set - the key is absent rather than null, so a mapper that reads it unconditionally throws on the common case. Keeping the mapping pure and separate from the fetch is what makes the dateless and archived cases testable without a live board, and confines the I/O to a thin shell; the live round-trip is covered by the walking skeleton in phase 04, not by a unit test here. Reuse the connector's existing client construction (GetJiraRestClientAsync / GetOrCreateClient around L1796-1870) rather than building a new HttpClient. CA1869: if the reader needs JsonSerializerOptions, cache it in a static readonly field. NUnit2045: independent asserts go inside using (Assert.EnterMultipleScope()), and because the rule judges the method, a private assertion helper needs its own scope. CA1861: hoist any inline new[]{} used in assertions.

steps.name: Ask Jira which Features carry a Release
steps.scenario_name: A Release resolves to the reference ids of the work that carries it
criteria: ResolveMany issues a single JQL fixVersion in (...) query keyed on the numeric version id, never on the version name, and returns one verdict per requested reference.
One call covers every requested reference, so the cost of a pass stays constant in the number of bound Deliveries rather than growing with it.
A version that is gone resolves to NotFound; a version carrying no date resolves to NoDate; a read that could not be made resolves to Unavailable and never to NotFound.
The verdict is the closed DeliverySourceResolution set already on disk, so a failed read is not representable as a deleted source.
Snapshots cross the port as reference ids only; no Feature or other domain object is handed back by the adapter.
The identity sweep is untouched and still runs SweepFields of key and updated only.
The existing JQL construction and encoding path in the connector is reused as is, because it is the injection control and must not be re-implemented.
steps.implementation_notes: This lands in slice 01a rather than slice 02 because the preview in step 02-02 needs exactly this membership read, and a preview-only path would spell the same fixVersion query a second time and leave one of the two to delete later. What slice 02 still owns is untouched: DeliverySourceSyncService, the PortfolioUpdater wiring, RecordableDeliveries, and the broken-source transition table. Unavailable is a member of the result set rather than a thrown exception precisely so a network blip cannot be mistaken for a deleted Release; route the transient arm deliberately and never collapse it into a catch alongside NotFound. The delta line assigning the resolve adapter to slice 02 sits inside the section marked SUPERSEDED and kept for the record, so it is not a live commitment. S1192: hoist repeated JQL fragments behind a const.

phases.name: Three routes a Portfolio owner can call

steps.name: DeliverySourcesController lists the sources and their options
steps.scenario_name: A Portfolio on a non-Jira connection is told it has no delivery sources rather than handed an error
criteria: A new DeliverySourcesController carries both the api/v1/portfolios/{portfolioId:int}/delivery-sources route and the api/latest equivalent.
GET on the collection requires PortfolioRead, is not premium-gated, and returns a list of key and displayName pairs.
The collection returns an empty list, not an error, for AzureDevOps, Linear, ServiceNow and CSV connections.
GET {sourceKey}/options requires PortfolioWrite and returns id, name and an optional date, with the date absent where Jira has none.
An unknown or unoffered sourceKey returns 404.
DeliverySourceDto lives in API/DTO/ and carries no persistence concern.
The controller constructor stays at seven parameters or fewer.
Delivery.cs, DeliveriesController.cs and DeliverySection.tsx are not touched, and no migration and no new enum member is created.
steps.implementation_notes: DeliveryRulesController is the nesting precedent: it declares the same dual v1/latest route pair at :14-15 over api/v1/portfolios/{portfolioId:int}/delivery-rules, and its GetSchema/Validate pair is the shape to mirror. These routes get their own controller precisely because DeliveriesController is already at eight constructor parameters behind an S107 suppression - do not add to it. The empty-list degradation is the behaviour, not an omission: a Portfolio whose connection is not Jira must get 200 with an empty list so the frontend simply renders no extra tab. Nothing is persisted anywhere in this slice. If registering the controller requires a Program.cs edit, note that Program.cs changes force the full backend Integration suite to run, so budget the time. CA1859 applies to every new private helper.

steps.name: Offer only Releases still worth forecasting
steps.scenario_name: Only an unreleased Release is offered
criteria: GetOptions offers only unreleased Releases. Both an archived Release and a Release already marked released are absent from the result.
The existing specs asserting an archived Release and a released Release come back selectable-or-not are inverted, not deleted: each now asserts absence.

A dateless Release is still returned, still unselectable, still carrying NoDateSet. Hiding the other two does not make the block reasons symmetric: a missing date is fixable from Jira and the reader should see it, whereas archived and released are both statements that this Release is finished with.
DeliverySourceBindability is untouched, still answers RetiredAtSource and still does NOT block released, and DeliverySourceBindabilityTest.cs is not edited at all.
A Delivery already bound to a Release keeps resolving after that Release is marked released. Hiding it from the picker must not retire a live binding, and a spec pins that.
ResolveMany no longer constructs an option with a blank project. Every Release it resolves carries the project it came from.
ResolveMany reads through the same cross-project enumeration GetOptions uses, so resolving many bound Deliveries costs one project sweep plus one membership search rather than one read per Delivery.
A credential that cannot list projects at all degrades to an answer rather than failing the whole endpoint, and a spec covers it.
steps.implementation_notes: TWO MAINTAINER RULINGS, 2026-08-23, both overriding the earlier acceptance criterion. (1) An archived Release is hidden rather than listed-and-labelled. (2) A Release already marked released is hidden too, because a shipped Release does not need a forecast. Net effect: the picker offers only unreleased Releases. The query is GET rest/api/3/project/{key}/version?maxResults=50&status=unreleased. Verified live on the demo instance with status=released,unreleased: HTTP 200 in 277ms, total=3 for LGHTHSDMO. That is the PAGINATED endpoint - the body is an object with values, total, isLast and startAt, not the bare array project/{key}/versions returns - so follow isLast, because a long-lived project can carry hundreds of versions. A dateless Release stays visible, and the asymmetry is worth one plain-language comment: a missing date is something the reader can go and fix, while archived and released both say this Release is finished with. THE SERVER MUST STILL ALLOW A RELEASED RELEASE TO BIND AND KEEP SYNCING. Hiding is presentation only. A Delivery bound to a Release that is later marked released must keep resolving, or marking a version released in Jira would silently break a live Delivery - the two lifecycles are meant to be independent. Do not add released to the bindability rule. Note the demo instance has released=false on all eight of its versions, so the live walking skeleton cannot observe this filter at all. Unit specs are the only cover; do not let a green E2E be mistaken for proof. The blank project comes from ReadOneRelease, which reads a bound Release by id and never learns its project. Moving ResolveMany onto the shared enumeration fixes that and the per-Delivery call cost in one change. The project-listing gap is real and uncovered: ReadVisibleProjects calls EnsureSuccessStatusCode, so a credential that cannot run project/search fails the whole endpoint while a single failing project degrades gracefully. Make the two consistent and pin it. Latency budget, from the maintainer: this runs when someone sets up a Delivery, not on every page load, so seconds are fine. No project-count cap, no narrow-by-project branch.

steps.name: Preview answers with the date and the Features that would come along
steps.scenario_name: A Release that matches no Feature in this Portfolio says why the list is empty
criteria: POST {sourceKey}/preview requires PortfolioWrite plus Premium and returns name, date and features shaped so the existing Feature grid renders it unchanged.
Membership comes from the resolver, which delegates to the adapter ResolveMany built in step 01-04; the preview issues no query of its own.
The returned reference ids are intersected with portfolio.Features on ReferenceId in the domain, so a Feature the Portfolio does not track never appears.
The preview response carries a discriminator saying why a feature list is empty, distinguishing a Release with no matching work from a Release whose work this Portfolio does not track.
The connector's existing JQL construction and encoding path is reused as is - it is the injection control and must not be re-implemented.
The identity sweep is untouched and still runs SweepFields of key and updated only.
Nothing is persisted: no Delivery is written, updated or archived by this route.
A Release that is gone and a Release the remote could not be asked about are answered distinctly, never as the same thing.

An empty match answers 200 with the reason, NOT 400. The route this one mirrors returns BadRequest on an empty list; copying that would turn the explicit empty state into an error and defeat the criterion the slice turns on.
steps.implementation_notes: SETTLED, and the crafter should not re-open it: the resolver delegates to IDeliverySourceProvider.ResolveMany, which step 01-04 implements. The preview does NOT issue its own membership query. The reasoning is that the resolver contract is to intersect remote membership with the Features the Portfolio actually tracks, which is exactly what the preview needs, so a preview-only path would spell the fixVersion query twice. The route to mirror for the response shape is delivery-rules/validate on DeliveryRulesController (Validate at :41-70), which already returns the Feature list the preview grid consumes; reusing it is why no new grid is needed. The membership query is a DIFFERENT query from the identity sweep, and widening the sweep to carry fixVersion would change what every refresh fetches for every customer. Nothing is persisted by this route. S1192: hoist the source key and the JQL fragments behind consts. MIRROR THE SHAPE, NOT THE STATUS: DeliveryRulesController.Validate at :63-68 returns BadRequest(matchingFeatures) when the list is empty. Reuse its response TYPE - List<FeatureDto>, built as new FeatureDto(feature, clock, blackoutPeriods, isBlocked, null) - so the existing grid renders it unchanged. Do NOT reuse its empty-list status. A Release matching nothing is a normal, expected answer that must arrive as 200 carrying a reason. The premium attribute is [LicenseGuard(RequirePremium = true)] and the scope attribute is [RbacGuard(RbacGuardRequirement.PortfolioWrite, ScopeIdRouteKey = "portfolioId")], both as used on that same Validate action. PROGRAM.CS IS SANCTIONED FOR THIS STEP, and only this one. The resolver needs AddScoped<IDeliverySourceResolver, DeliverySourceResolver>() beside the neighbours at Program.cs:1191-1240; there is no way to inject it otherwise. Know the consequence before you make the edit: Scripts/test-selection/path-classifier.sh:22 counts Program.cs as a shared path, so CI will run EVERY connector integration category on this change - Jira, Azure DevOps, Linear, ServiceNow and GitHub - not just the Jira one the connector edits already trigger. That is the classifier being deliberately conservative about the DI graph, not a fault. Do NOT run those categories locally to compensate: they hit real instances, and the Linear key is shared with CI, so a local run can rate-limit the next CI build. Keep using the exclusion filter.

steps.name: Drive the three routes over HTTP
steps.scenario_name: The three delivery-source routes answer over HTTP on both api/v1 and api/latest
criteria: An abstract harness plus a Scenarios and Specifications partial pair follows the QuietWriteBack precedent exactly.
All three routes are exercised end to end through WebApplicationFactory, on both the api/v1 and the api/latest prefix.
The empty-list degradation is proven for all four non-Jira systems: AzureDevOps, Linear, ServiceNow and CSV.
The 404 for an unknown or unoffered source key is proven over HTTP, not only at the controller.
A PortfolioRead caller can list sources and is refused on options and preview.
A non-premium caller is refused on preview and still allowed on the collection.

The IDeliverySourceProvider capability is faked at the connector boundary while the controller, routing and RBAC pipeline stay real, and the harness names that fake explicitly rather than burying it in a setup helper.
No test in this step is decorated with a live-connector Category.
steps.implementation_notes: Infrastructure policy for this slice is inherit: WebApplicationFactory for the driving port, real EF for driven-internal, Mock<IWorkTrackingConnector> for the tracker. The one genuinely new policy row is the IDeliverySourceProvider capability - it is faked at the connector boundary, which is the honest place, because the alternative is either a live board in the unit pass or a controller that is no longer the thing under test. There is no infrastructure-policy document in this feature workspace today; if DISTILL's policy table turns out to live somewhere in the workspace, add the row there rather than creating a new file for it, and say where you put it. Follow Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/API/Integration/QuietWriteBack/: QuietWriteBackAcceptanceTest.cs is the abstract harness, and Slice01WriteBackCollectionScenarios.cs / Slice01WriteBackCollectionSpecifications.cs are the partial pair - Scenarios holds arrange-and-act, Specifications holds the named assertions. NUnit2045 judges the METHOD, so a shared private assertion helper needs its own using (Assert.EnterMultipleScope()). CA1869: cache JsonSerializerOptions in a static readonly field - this is exactly where that rule lands in test helpers. CA1861: hoist inline new[]{} assertion arrays. This is a git worktree, so the pre-commit ledger hook diffs the main checkout's empty index and passes vacuously - treat it as absent and run dotnet build, the filtered dotnet test and the dotnet format analyzers sweep by hand. PRECEDENT, verified: QuietWriteBackAcceptanceTest.cs is an abstract base holding TestWebApplicationFactory<Program>, an HttpClient, and Mock fields, with per-slice Scenarios/Specifications partial pairs beside it. Real EF over SQLite plus the real routing and RBAC pipeline; faked connector, faked licence service. ONE DIFFERENCE THAT MATTERS: that harness fakes Mock<IWorkTrackingConnector>, but the delivery-source capability is declared on IJiraWorkTrackingConnector, which composes IWorkTrackingConnector with IDeliverySourceProvider. A Mock<IWorkTrackingConnector> cannot stand in for it. Fake at the level the capability actually lives, and make sure whatever resolves a connector per connection hands back the faked Jira one. If wiring this needs an edit to Program.cs, STOP and say so before making it: a Program.cs change pulls the whole backend Integration suite into the run, which drags in the live-connector tests and their flake exposure. That is a decision to surface, not to absorb.

phases.name: The Jira Release tab in the Create Delivery modal

steps.name: Boundary parsers for the delivery source payloads
steps.scenario_name: A Release option with no release date parses to a source with no date rather than an invalid one
criteria: DeliverySource.ts parses its boundary with Zod, matching ArchivedDelivery.ts, the sibling in the same folder.

A Release with no release date parses to a source carrying no date. It is NOT run through z.coerce.date(), which turns null into 1970 and would render the commonest case as a Release dated fifty years ago instead of one needing a date set.
Nullable backend fields use .nullable() or .nullish().transform, never .optional(): a C# T? serialises to JSON null, which .optional() does not accept and which hard-fails the parse.
An absent date field parses to a source carrying no date; it is not coerced to an invalid Date and does not throw.
A malformed payload is rejected at the boundary rather than propagating an unusable object into the component tree.
The empty-preview reason is modelled as a closed set, so an unrecognised reason is caught here and never rendered raw.
The parsers are pure, so the specs need no rendering harness.
steps.implementation_notes: CORRECTED AFTER A DESIGN ERROR, verified against the tree: DESIGN told this step to hand-roll asObject/asDate parsers because Zod was still gated. Both halves are false. zod ^4.4.3 is a real dependency, 21 files under src/models use it, and the gate condition (TypeScript 6 / Vite 8) is met and exceeded by the installed TypeScript 7.0.2 and Vite 8.2.1. The hand-rolled idiom DESIGN named as the house pattern exists in exactly one file, DeliveryMetricsHistory.ts; the direct sibling ArchivedDelivery.ts in models/Delivery uses Zod. Follow the sibling. The date field is the trap worth spelling out: DeliverySourceOption.Date is nullable and absent whenever Jira has no releaseDate, which slice 00 measured as two of three Releases on the demo instance. z.coerce.date() silently turns null into the 1970 epoch, so a dateless Release would render as dated rather than as needing a date - defeating the acceptance criterion this whole slice turns on. Guard it explicitly and prove it with a spec.

steps.name: DeliveryService reaches the three routes
steps.scenario_name: Listing delivery sources for a non-Jira Portfolio yields an empty list and no error
criteria: IDeliveryService gains getDeliverySources, getDeliverySourceOptions and previewDeliverySource, and DeliveryService implements them.
Each method routes its response through the parsers from the previous step; no raw payload escapes the service.
An empty source list is a normal answer that resolves, never a rejection.
A 404 on an unknown source key surfaces as a distinguishable failure, not as an empty list.
createMockDeliveryService is extended so every existing consumer of the mock still type-checks.
pnpm test green, pnpm build with zero errors and zero warnings, Biome clean.
steps.implementation_notes: IDeliveryService is declared at DeliveryService.ts:50 and the mock factory createMockDeliveryService at src/tests/MockApiServiceProvider.ts:391 - both must move together or the whole frontend suite fails to compile. Follow the existing method bodies in the same file for error handling and base-path construction rather than inventing a new convention; validateRules at :183-199 is the closest sibling to previewDeliverySource. Conflating a 404 with an empty list is the failure mode to avoid: they mean opposite things to the user, one is a configuration problem and the other is a Release with nothing in it.

steps.name: DeliverySourceTab renders the picker and the preview
steps.scenario_name: A dateless Release cannot be picked, a Community licence sees the tab gated, and a non-Jira Portfolio sees no tab at all
criteria: The Jira Release tab appears in the descriptor list only when the Portfolio's connection offers a source; on the four non-Jira systems no extra tab is rendered at all.
Picking a dated Release shows its date and the Features that would come along, using the Feature grid that already exists.

A dateless Release is listed but not selectable and says what is missing. Archived and released Releases never reach the picker at all - the server filters them - so the tab needs no client-side handling for either, and must not invent any.

On a Community licence the Jira Release tab is visible and carries a premium notice; it is neither hidden nor absent, which is why the source-list route is deliberately not premium-gated. Proven by mocking useLicenseRestrictions to return canUsePremiumFeatures false, the way DeliveryCreateModal.test.tsx:37 already does, and asserting both that the tab renders and that the notice is shown.
A second source reported by the server renders as a further tab with no frontend change, so the list is genuinely server-driven rather than a two-way branch with a third arm bolted on.
Selectability is rendered from the server's answer and never recomputed in TypeScript.
An empty preview explains itself using the reason the server sent, in the user's configured terminology for Features.
The tab performs no save and offers no persistence affordance - nothing it does survives closing the modal.
The three pre-existing DeliveryCreateModal suites still pass.
pnpm test green, pnpm build with zero errors and zero warnings, Biome clean.

The premium notice on this tab names Release-based selection. The existing PremiumFeatureNotice at DeliveryCreateModal.tsx:73-77 hardcodes the sentence about rule-based selection, so reusing it unchanged would tell the reader the wrong thing; parameterise it or add a sibling rather than sharing the wrong copy.

The non-Jira case is asserted directly at component level and not merely inherited from the API contract: rendering with a connection that offers no sources shows exactly the two built-in tabs and no third one.

The Release list shows a loading state while it fills, and groups options by their Jira project so two Releases sharing a name stay distinguishable. Measured on the demo instance: Release 44 and Release 45 exist in both JUSTATEST and PROJ with different ids, so a flat list would render two identical labels.
steps.implementation_notes: The greying-out is presentation of a server decision, not a client rule: the server already refuses to bind what the picker greys out, so the tab must render the bindability answer rather than recomputing archived, released and date logic client-side. Duplicating that rule is how the two drift, and the drift is invisible until someone binds a Release the picker said they could not. User-facing copy uses the Terminology-configurable words seeded in TerminologySeeder.cs - Feature and Features, never Epic or Story - but Jira Release is a literal Jira concept and stays as written. The descriptor list from step 00-01 is the only place the tab is registered; if registering it needs a change to DeliveryCreateModal beyond consuming the list, the precursor refactor was incomplete and should be extended rather than worked around. DeliverySection.tsx stays untouched - persistence is slice 01b. LATENCY IS ACCEPTABLE HERE, per the maintainer: binding a Release happens when someone sets up a Delivery, not on every page load, so a second or two while the list fills is fine. Do NOT build a project-count cap, a narrow-by-project branch or a threshold warning - none of that is wanted. A loading state plus a per-connection cache for the modal lifetime is the whole requirement. Measured cost on the demo instance: 1 call for the project list plus one per project, 7 projects, about 1.6s serial and well under a second in parallel.

phases.name: Prove it against the real board

steps.name: Walking skeleton against the live demo Jira
steps.scenario_name: Picking a dated Jira Release shows its date and the Features it would bring
criteria: One walking-skeleton-tagged spec, happy path only: connect Jira, open Create Delivery, see the Jira Release tab, pick a dated Release, see its date and the matching Features.
The spec names specific real work items so the assertion is a fact rather than a reading of whatever the board holds today.
Every interaction goes through a Page Object; there is no inline page.locator() in the spec.
The spec is run locally against the live instance before it is committed, never committed unrun.
No second spec is added for the unhappy paths - those are already covered at the HTTP and component levels.
The spec binds to LGHTHSDMO version 10006, which is not archived and whose membership is stable.
The preview asserts four Features, not five: four Epics carry the version and so does one Story, and the Story is not tracked at Feature level, so it must be absent from the preview.
JiraSystemUpdater.py sets that version release date to a fixed offset ahead of the day it runs, so every nightly run leaves the date roughly a month out no matter how many runs preceded it.
The date roll is idempotent: it never adds a month to whatever it finds, which would compound to a year out after a year of runs.
The nightly Auto-Generated issues do not acquire the version, so the preview count is a fact rather than a reading of last night run.
steps.implementation_notes: Fixture confirmed by the maintainer: https://letpeoplework.atlassian.net/projects/LGHTHSDMO/versions/10006 - four Epics (LGHTHSDMO-7 through LGHTHSDMO-10) plus one Story carry it, and none of those items move, so the count is stable. Verify the exact issue keys against the board before asserting on them. The Story is the valuable half of this fixture: membership matches at the level Lighthouse tracks and never rolls up from children, so an item the Portfolio does not track as a Feature simply is not in the Release. Asserting four rather than five is what proves that against real data instead of a mock. The Portfolio the spec creates must use a query that actually contains those four Epics, or the intersection is empty and the spec silently exercises the empty-state path rather than the happy path. Model the spec on tests/specs/features/FeatureDependencies.spec.ts, which names specific real work items for the same reason. Live Jira credentials come from TestConfig.JiraToken as tests/specs/jira/jira.spec.ts already does. Run it locally against the live instance before committing; never commit an unrun spec or POM locator. Note the Jira API key is shared with CI, so avoid repeated exploratory runs.

slice_01b.item: The options list must always include the currently-bound Release, even when the unreleased-only filter would exclude it.
slice_01b.why: Slice 01a hides archived and released Releases from the picker, but a binding survives its Release being marked released or archived. Once 01b persists bindings, editing such a Delivery fetches options that do not contain its own current value, so the control renders with nothing selected and a save can silently unbind or switch it. Filter the choices, never the current value.
slice_01b.cannot_bite_yet: Slice 01a persists nothing, so no bound Delivery exists to edit.
slice_01b.raised: 2026-08-23, maintainer discussion of the unreleased-only ruling

slice_01b.item: DeliverySourceUnavailableReason has no member meaning a transient read failure; ResolveMany currently reports CapabilityWithdrawn.
slice_01b.why: Nothing reads it yet and the design says a higher layer must never persist broken-source on Unavailable regardless, so it is harmless today. Slice 02 builds the transition table that actually consumes it and should settle the vocabulary then.

slice_01b.item: The auto-filled Delivery Date is the browser local rendering of a UTC instant, so west of UTC it names the day before the one Jira holds.
slice_01b.why: Slice 01a only displays it, and the field and the preview beside it agree, which is why it was built this way. Slice 01b persists that value - at which point a viewer in a negative-offset zone saves a date one day earlier than the Release actually carries. This is the calendar-day-versus-instant rule the codebase has been bitten by before: anything reducing an instant to a day must name the zone it reduces in.
slice_01b.note: All three test suites are pinned to Europe/Zurich, so no existing test can see it. Pre-existing in LocalDateTimeDisplay; new only in that it now reaches a saveable field.

fix_in_refactor_phase.item: GetOptions caches an incomplete sweep for 5 minutes, so one transient 500 on a single project poisons the picker for that long.
fix_in_refactor_phase.origin: introduced in 02-01 with the 5-minute cache, surfaced by 02-02 which added sweep-completeness tracking
fix_in_refactor_phase.fix: the sweep already carries SawEverything; do not cache a sweep that did not see everything, or cache it with a much shorter life. A spec should pin that a poisoned entry is not served.
fix_in_refactor_phase.why_not_done_inline: unspecified at the time and outside 02-02 criteria; fixing it silently would have been worse than flagging it

fix_in_refactor_phase.item: IDeliverySourceResolver return type changed from IReadOnlyDictionary<string, DeliverySourceResolution> to PortfolioSourcePreview during 02-03.
fix_in_refactor_phase.why: The dictionary could not satisfy the empty-reason discriminator: once membership is narrowed to the Portfolio, nothing-tagged and tagged-but-not-tracked are the same empty list. The interface had zero implementations and zero callers at the time, so nothing broke.
fix_in_refactor_phase.action: No fix owed. Recorded because the interface was landed by DISTILL and the change is worth a reviewer seeing rather than discovering.

orchestrator_notes.s3236_phrasing: Write S3236 as: pass ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(key) and NEVER ThrowIfNull(key, nameof(key)) - the second parameter is CallerArgumentExpression and the compiler fills it, so passing nameof by hand is the error. An earlier dispatch phrased this as ThrowIfNull(key) without nameof, which parses both ways and cost a build cycle in step 02-03.
